s.n: Mrs Edgecomb's cornbread with honey butter
s.note: Wild Bill only wanted a little corn bread. Skillet cornbread, whipped honey butter.
s.how: Heat a 23cm cast iron pan in a 220C oven with 20g of the butter in it. Whisk the dry ingredients with a good pinch of salt, then whisk in the buttermilk, eggs and 100g melted butter. Pour into the hot pan and bake until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Beat the soft butter with the honey and salt flakes and serve with the warm cornbread.
shop: 120g butter, plus 80g soft butter for the honey butter@Dairy

s.n: Cornmeal fried okra with comeback sauce
s.note: John Coffey's last meal had okra. Crisp cornmeal okra, spicy comeback sauce.
s.how: Stir the mayonnaise, tomato sauce, hot sauce and a squeeze of lemon into a comeback sauce. Soak the okra in the buttermilk while you mix the cornmeal, flour, paprika and salt. Toss the okra in the cornmeal mix to coat well. Fry in batches in oil at 180C until crisp and golden, then drain and salt. Serve hot with the sauce.

s.n: Mr Jingles' pimento cheese and crackers
s.note: Mr Jingles is somehow still alive. Sharp cheddar, roast capsicum, crackers.
s.how: Beat the cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth. Fold in the cheddar, capsicum, paprika and hot sauce and season with pepper. Pile into a bowl and serve with the crackers and celery.

m.n: Last meal meatloaf with mash and gravy
m.note: The meal before John walks the Mile. Glazed meatloaf, buttery mash, onion gravy.
m.how: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk, then mix with the mince, grated onion, egg, thyme and plenty of salt and pepper. Shape into a loaf on a lined tray, stir the tomato sauce, sugar and vinegar together and brush half over. Bake at 180C for 1 hour, brushing on the rest of the glaze halfway, then rest it. Boil the potatoes until tender, then mash with half the butter and a splash of the milk. Fry the sliced onion in the rest of the butter until brown, stir in the flour, then whisk in the stock and simmer into gravy. Wilt the silverbeet in a hot pan, slice the meatloaf thickly and serve with the mash, gravy and greens.
shop: 1 brown onion, grated, plus 1 sliced for the gravy@Produce

w.n: Top Hat peach cobbler with vanilla ice cream
w.note: John's first picture show is Top Hat. Bubbling spiced peaches, buttermilk biscuit crust.
w.how: Toss the peaches with the brown sugar, cinnamon, cornflour and lemon juice in a baking dish. Rub the butter into the flour and caster sugar, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Drop spoonfuls of dough over the peaches, leaving gaps for the juice to bubble through. Bake at 190C until the topping is golden and the fruit is bubbling. Rest for 5 minutes and serve warm with the ice cream.

d.note: A floor the colour of faded limes. Lime, mint, raw sugar and soda.
d.how: Heat the sugar and water with strips of lime peel until dissolved, then cool and strain. Squeeze the limes and stir the juice into the syrup. Pour over ice and mint in 4 glasses and top with soda.
